extracted.intended_audience: Federal Communications Commission staff, legal counsel, complainants and members of the public interacting with FCC accessibility and debt-collection procedures (including persons with disabilities and entities subject to FCC claims collection)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards governing FCC programs' accessibility under Section 504 (definitions, procedural requirements, accessibility policies, complaint handling, facility and employment provisions) and rules for administrative collection of claims owed to the United States (definitions, exceptions, collection procedures, and effects on applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary aids
rubrics_metrics.description: means services or devices that enable persons with impaired sensory, manual, or speaking skills to have an equal opportunity to participate in, and enjoy the benefits of, programs or activities conducted by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: for vision-impaired — readers, Brailled materials, audio recordings; for hearing-impaired — telephone handset amplifiers, telephones compatible with hearing aids, TTY/TDDs, interpreters, CART, captioning, notetakers, written materials, and similar services/devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: means Federal Communications Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: means a written statement, or a complaint in audio, Braille, electronic, and/or video format, that contains the complainant's name and address and describes the Commission's alleged discriminatory action in sufficient detail to inform the Commission of the nature and date of the alleged violation of section 504.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be signed by the complainant or authorized person on print complaints. Audio/Braille/electronic/video complaints must contain an affirmative identity statement functionally equivalent to a signature. Complaints filed on behalf of classes/third parties shall describe or identify alleged victims by name if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility
rubrics_metrics.description: means all or any portion of buildings, structures, equipment, roads, walks, parking lots, or other real or personal property.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: means the General Counsel of the Federal Communications Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual with a disability — physical or mental impairment (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical or mental impairment includes, but is not limited to, any physiological disorder/condition, cosmetic disfigurement, or anatomical loss affecting specified body systems, and mental or psychological disorders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated examples: neurological; musculoskeletal; special sense organs; respiratory; cardiovascular; reproductive; digestive; genitourinary; hemic and lymphatic; skin; endocrine; mental retardation; organic brain syndrome; emotional/mental illness; specific learning disabilities; diseases such as cerebral palsy, epilepsy, muscular dystrophy, multiple sclerosis, cancer, heart disease, diabetes, drug addiction and alcoholism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual with a disability — major life activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Major life activities include functions such as caring for one's self, performing manual tasks, walking, seeing, hearing, speaking, breathing, learning, and working.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual with a disability — has a record of such an impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: Means has a history of, or has been misclassified as having, a mental or physical impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual with a disability — is regarded as having an impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: Means (i) has an impairment that does not substantially limit major life activities but is treated by the Commission as such; (ii) has an impairment that limits major life activities only due to attitudes of others; or (iii) has none of the impairments defined but is treated as having such impairment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Director
rubrics_metrics.description: means the individual delegated authority as described in 47 CFR 0.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs or Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: mean any activity of the Commission permitted or required by its enabling statutes, including but not limited to any licensing or certification program, proceeding, investigation, hearing, meeting, board or committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified individual with a disability (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who, with or without reasonable modification to rules, policies, or practices or the provision of auxiliary aids, meets the essential eligibility requirements for participation in the program or activity and can achieve the purpose of the program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three contexts provided: (1) where individual must perform services/achieve level of accomplishment; (2) other programs/activities — meets essential eligibility for participation or receipt of benefits; (3) employment definition per 29 CFR 1630.2(m) applies via §1.1840.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 504 (definition and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 ... As used in this part, section 504 applies only to programs or activities conducted by Executive agencies and not to federally assisted programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References statutory amendments and limits applicability to executive agency-conducted programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Communications Commission Section 504 Programs and Activities Accessibility Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: The Consumer & Governmental Affairs Bureau shall publish a 'Federal Communications Commission Section 504 Programs and Activities Accessibility Handbook' and update it at least every three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handbook available to public in hard copy on request and electronically; shall contain procedures for releasing documents, holding meetings, receiving comments, and other aspects of Commission programs to achieve accessibility. It is for internal staff use and public information only and is not intended to create enforceable rights or causes of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of compliance (frequency and participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall, beginning in 2004 and at least every three years thereafter, review its current policies and practices in view of advances in relevant technology and achievability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will modify practices/procedures based on review to ensure programs/activities are fully accessible. Interested persons, including individuals with disabilities or their organizations, may participate by submitting comments. Written comments must be signed or contain an affirmative identity statement for non-print formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of compliance — recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall maintain on file and make available for public inspection for four years following completion of the compliance review a description of areas examined and problems identified; all comments and complaints filed regarding compliance; and a description of any modifications made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall make available to employees, applicants, participants, beneficiaries, and other interested persons information regarding the regulations set forth in this part, and their applicability to the programs or activities conducted by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information shall be made available in such manner as the Section 504 Officer finds necessary to apprise persons of protections assured by section 504.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibitions against discrimination (§1.1830(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified individual with a disability shall, on the basis of disability, be excluded from participation in, be denied the benefits of, or otherwise be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity conducted by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminatory actions prohibited — list (§1.1830(b)(1)(i)-(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission, in providing any aid, benefit, or service, may not, directly or through arrangements, on the basis of disability: (i) deny opportunity to participate or benefit; (ii) afford unequal opportunity; (iii) provide an aid/benefit/service that is not as effective in affording equal opportunity to obtain same result; (iv) provide different/separate aid unless necessary to be as effective; (v) deny opportunity to participate as member of planning/advisory boards; (vi) otherwise limit enjoyment of any right/privilege/advantage/opportunity enjoyed by others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits both explicit and effective inequality in benefits/services and participation opportunities, including advisory roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exclusion even when equivalent separate programs exist (§1.1830(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may not deny a qualified individual with a disability the opportunity to participate in any program or activity even where the Commission is also providing equivalent permissibly separate or different programs or activities for persons with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited criteria or methods of administration (§1.1830(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may not utilize criteria or methods of administration that have the purpose or effect of subjecting qualified individuals to discrimination or defeating/substantially impairing accomplishment of the program's objectives with respect to individuals with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site or location selection prohibition (§1.1830(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may not, in determining the site or location of a facility, make selections that have the purpose or effect of excluding individuals with disabilities or defeating/substantially impairing program objectives with respect to such individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement contractor selection prohibition (§1.1830(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission, in the selection of procurement contractors, may not use criteria that subject qualified individuals with disabilities to discrimination on the basis of disability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing/certification programs non-discrimination (§1.1830(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may not administer a licensing or certification program in a manner that subjects qualified individuals with disabilities to discrimination, nor establish requirements for programs/activities of licensees or certified entities that subject qualified individuals with disabilities to discrimination; however, programs/activities of entities licensed/certified by the Commission are not themselves covered by this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modifications requirement and fundamental alteration defense (§1.1830(b)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall make reasonable modifications in policies, practices, or procedures when necessary to avoid discrimination unless the Commission can demonstrate that making the modifications would fundamentally alter the nature of the program, service, or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Commission alleges fundamental alteration or undue burdens, it bears the burden of proving it and the Managing Director (with Section 504 Officer consultation) must make the decision and produce a written statement of reasons. If compliance would result in alteration/burdens, the Commission must take other actions that do not result in such alteration/burdens but still ensure individuals with disabilities receive benefits/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/executive-order-limited programs excluded (§1.1830(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: This part does not prohibit exclusion of persons without disabilities from programs limited by Federal statute or Executive order to individuals with disabilities, or exclusion of a specific class of individuals with disabilities from a program limited to a different class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most integrated setting requirement (§1.1830(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall administer programs and activities in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of qualified individuals with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment non-discrimination and applicable procedures (§1.1840)
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified individual with a disability shall, on the basis of disability, be subjected to discrimination in employment under any program or activity conducted by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions, requirements and procedures of section 501 of the Rehabilitation Act and EEOC regulations in 29 CFR parts 1614 and 1630, Basic Negotiated Agreement, and Subchapter III of the Civil Service Reform Act apply to employment in federally conducted programs or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility: discrimination prohibited due to inaccessible facilities (§1.1849(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided in §1.1850, no qualified individual shall, because the Commission's facilities are inaccessible to, or unusable by, individuals with disabilities, be denied benefits, excluded from participation, or otherwise subjected to discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility requests process and advance notice (§1.1849(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals shall request accessibility by contacting the Commission's Section 504 Officer per the FCC Section 504 Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission will make every effort to provide accommodations requiring assistance (ASL interpreters, CART, transcribers, captioners, readers) if request is made at least five business days in advance. For requests made fewer than five business days before an event, Commission will make every effort but may be less likely to secure services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility for existing facilities — general obligation and exceptions (§1.1850(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall operate each program/activity so that, when viewed in its entirety, it is readily accessible and usable by individuals with disabilities, but this does not necessarily require making each existing facility accessible, nor require actions that would fundamentally alter the nature of a program/activity or cause undue financial/administrative burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Commission personnel believe a proposed action would fundamentally alter the program or cause undue burdens, the Commission must demonstrate that and the Managing Director (with Section 504 Officer) must issue a written decision after considering all Commission resources; if such alteration/burden exists, Commission must take other effective actions that do not cause such alteration/burdens but still ensure access to benefits/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to achieve program accessibility (§1.1850(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may comply through redesign of equipment, reassignment of services to accessible buildings, assignment of aides, home visits, delivery of services at alternate accessible sites, alteration of existing facilities, construction of new facilities, or other methods resulting in accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural changes are not required where other methods are effective. When altering buildings, Commission must meet accessibility requirements compelled by the Architectural Barriers Act. Prioritize methods offering programs in the most integrated setting appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for program accessibility compliance (§1.1850(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall comply with obligations within sixty (60) days of the effective date of this subpart, except that structural changes shall be made within three (3) years of the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan requirements (§1.1850(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If structural changes will be undertaken, the Commission shall develop within six (6) months a transition plan setting forth steps necessary to complete changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must provide opportunity for interested persons to participate via comments. Plan shall at minimum: (1) identify physical obstacles limiting accessibility; (2) describe methods to make facilities accessible; (3) specify schedule for steps and, if longer than 1 year, identify annual steps; (4) indicate official responsible for implementation. Copy of plan available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building accessibility: new construction and alterations (§1.1851)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each building or part of a building constructed or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of the Commission shall be designed, constructed, or altered so as to be readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions, requirements and standards of the Architectural Barriers Act (42 U.S.C. 4151-4157) and implementing regulations in 41 CFR 102-76.60 to 102-76.95 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance procedures — scope (§1.1870(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies to all allegations of discrimination on the basis of disability in programs or activities conducted by the Commission, except as provided in paragraph (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment complaint procedures governed by EEOC (§1.1870(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints alleging violations with respect to employment shall be processed according to procedures established by the EEOC in 29 CFR part 1614 pursuant to section 501 of the Rehabilitation Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address for filing complaints (§1.1870(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints alleging violation of section 504 with respect to the Commission's programs and activities shall be addressed to the Managing Director and filed with the Office of the Secretary at the FCC's main office (address in 47 CFR 0.401(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of complaints — jurisdiction and timeliness (§1.1870(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall accept and investigate all complete complaints for which it has jurisdiction. All such complaints must be filed within 180 days of the alleged act of discrimination; the Commission may extend this time period for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete complaints — notice and dismissal (§1.1870(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission receives an incomplete complaint, the complainant will be notified within 30 days that additional information is needed; if not completed within 30 days of that notice, the Commission shall dismiss the complaint without prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of complaints outside FCC jurisdiction (§1.1870(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission receives a complaint over which it does not have jurisdiction, it shall promptly notify the complainant and make reasonable efforts to refer the complaint to the appropriate government entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify U.S. Access Board on building accessibility complaints (§1.1870(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall notify the United States Access Board upon receipt of any complaint alleging that a building or facility subject to the Architectural Barriers Act is not readily accessible or usable by individuals with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation results and remedies notice within 180 days (§1.1870(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days of receipt of a complete complaint for which it has jurisdiction, the Commission shall notify the complainant of the results of the investigation in a letter containing findings of fact and conclusions of law, a description of a remedy for each violation found, and a notice of the right to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals deadlines and processing (§1.1870(h)-(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals of findings or remedies must be filed by the complainant within 90 days of receipt of the Commission's letter; timely appeals processed by Office of the Secretary. The Commission shall notify the complainant of results of the appeal within 60 days of receipt of the appeal; if additional information is requested, Commission has 60 days from receipt of that information to determine the appeal. Time limits may be extended with permission of the General Counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of investigation authority (§1.1870(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may delegate its authority for conducting complaint investigations to other federal agencies, except that authority for making the final determination may not be delegated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart O — administrative offset definition (§1.1901(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term administrative offset means withholding money payable by the United States Government to, or held by the Government for, a person, organization, or entity to satisfy a debt the person, organization, or entity owes the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart O — agency/Commission definition (§1.1901(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term agency or Commission means the Federal Communications Commission (including USF, TRS Fund, and other reporting components) or any other agency of the U.S. Government as defined by section 105 of title 5 U.S.C., the U.S. Postal Service, Postal Rate Commission, military departments, judicial/legislative branch agencies, including the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency head
rubrics_metrics.description: The term agency head means the Chairperson of the Federal Communications Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application (broadly defined)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term application includes, in addition to petitions and applications elsewhere defined in the Commission's rules, any request, as for assistance, relief, declaratory ruling, or decision, by the Commission or on delegated authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim and debt (definition and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms claim and debt are synonymous and refer to an amount of money, funds, or property determined by an agency official to be due to the United States from any person/organization/entity (except another Federal agency) and, for administrative offset under 31 U.S.C. 3716, include amounts owed to the U.S. by states/territories and amounts owed on account of extension of credit or loans made by/insured/guaranteed by the U.S., fees, leases, rents, royalties, services, sales, overpayments, penalties, damages, interest, taxes, forfeitures issued after a notice of apparent liability partially paid or subject to a final court order, and similar sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes many categories; excludes amounts owed by another Federal agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creditor agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the agency to which the debt is owed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt collection center
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an agency or unit/subagency designated by the Secretary of the Treasury to collect debt owed to the United States (e.g., FMS, Fiscal Service, U.S. Treasury).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes written letters, orders, judgments, and memoranda from the Commission or on delegated authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delinquent (definition) (§1.1901(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a claim/debt not paid by the date specified by the agency unless satisfactory payment arrangements made, or at any time thereafter debtor has failed to satisfy an obligation under a payment agreement or instrument with the agency or pursuant to a Commission rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of this subpart, an installment payment under 47 CFR 1.2110(g) will not be considered delinquent until expiration of all applicable grace periods and other applicable periods under Commission rules to make the payment due. Rules in this subpart do not affect other Commission rules regarding payment for licenses or automatic cancellation provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposable pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Means that part of current basic pay, special pay, incentive pay, retired pay, retainer pay, or other authorized pay remaining after deduction of any amounts required by law to be withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must exclude certain deductions described in 5 CFR 581.105(b)-(f) to determine disposable pay subject to salary offset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a current employee of the Commission or of another agency, including a current member of the Armed Forces or a Reserve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes natural persons, legal associations, applicants, licensees, and regulatees.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCCS
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the Federal Claims Collection Standards jointly issued by the Secretary of the Treasury and the Attorney General (31 CFR parts 900-904).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paying agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the agency employing the individual and authorizing the payment of his or her current pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral for litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Means referral to the Department of Justice for appropriate legal proceedings except where the Commission has statutory authority to handle the litigation itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting component
rubrics_metrics.description: Means any program, account, or entity required to be included in the Agency's Financial Statements by GAAP for Federal Agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an administrative offset to collect a debt under 5 U.S.C. 5514 by deduction(s) at one or more officially established pay intervals from the current pay account of an employee without his or her consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the cancellation, remission, forgiveness, or non-recovery of a debt or fee, including debts due to the United States, by an entity or employee as permitted or required by specified statutes (e.g., 5 U.S.C. 5584, 10 U.S.C. 2774, 31 U.S.C. 3711).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of words (plural/singular and gender) (§1.1901(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: Words in the plural shall include the singular and vice-versa, masculine gender includes feminine and vice-versa; 'includes' and 'including' do not exclude matters not listed but do include matters of the same general class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to coverage — transportation account audits (§1.1902(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims arising from audit of transportation accounts pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3726 shall be determined/collected/compromised/terminated/settled in accordance with regulations under 31 U.S.C. 3726 (see 41 CFR part 102-118).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to coverage — acquisition contract claims and FAR (§1.1902(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims arising out of acquisition contracts subject to the FAR shall be determined/collected/compromised/terminated/settled in accordance with those regulations (48 CFR part 32). If not provided for in FAR, contract claims that were subject to contracting officer's final decision may be handled under this regulation, except no additional review beyond that provided by the contracting officer and interest/administrative/penalty amounts subject to contract limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to coverage — antitrust/fraud claims referred to DOJ (§1.1902(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims based wholly/partly on conduct violating antitrust laws, or indicating fraud/false claim/misrepresentation shall be referred to the Department of Justice as only DOJ has authority to compromise, suspend, or terminate collection action on such claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCC will apply FCCS standards for administrative collection only to the extent authorized by DOJ in a particular case. DOJ may at its discretion return the claim to the forwarding agency for further handling per FCCS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to coverage — tax claims excluded (§1.1902(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Tax claims are excluded from coverage of this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency claims negotiation (§1.1902(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will attempt to resolve interagency claims by negotiation in accordance with Executive Order 12146.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-supersession of other Commission rules (§1.1902(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this subpart supersedes or invalidates other Commission rules (e.g., Part 1 competitive bidding rules) regarding the Commission's rights including canceling a license, obtaining judgment, or collecting interest, penalties, and administrative costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of procedures singly or in combination (§1.1903)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures authorized by this regulation (including disclosure to consumer reporting agencies, contracting for collection services, administrative offset, salary offset) may be used singly or in combination so long as applicable law/regulation requirements are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance to law and regulations (§1.1904)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements of applicable law (31 U.S.C. 3701-3719 and amendments) have been implemented in government-wide standards including OPM regulations (5 CFR part 550) and FCCS (31 CFR parts 900-904).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every item in those standards is incorporated by reference; where circumstances are not covered, Commission will proceed in accordance with applicable requirements in the referred standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other procedures; collection of forfeiture penalties (§1.1905)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations do not require the Commission to duplicate administrative/other proceedings required by contract or other laws; they do not supersede procedures permitted/required by other statutes/regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary forfeitures imposed by the Commission governed initially by procedures in 47 U.S.C. 503, 504 and 47 CFR 1.80; after compliance with those procedures, Commission may determine collection under this subpart is appropriate but need not duplicate proceedings. Fees/penalties prescribed by law may be collected as permitted by applicable law; nothing restricts Commission from other rights to recover amounts owed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal action permitted (§1.1906)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in these regulations is intended to preclude utilization of informal administrative actions or remedies (including ADR) or for the Commission to exercise rights as agreed among the parties in written agreements (including notes and security agreements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of property or collateral (§1.1907)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this regulation is intended to deter the Commission from exercising any other right under law/regulation or agreement, or to exercise authority as a regulator under the Communications Act and the Commission's rules, in demanding return of specific property or, as a non-exclusive alternative, return of property or payment of its value or amount due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omissions not a defense (§1.1908)
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure or omission of the Commission to comply with any provision in this regulation shall not serve as a defense to any debtor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of insufficient fee payments, delinquent debts, or debarment — examination (§1.1910(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application or request subject to FRN requirement will be examined to determine if the applicant has paid appropriate fees, is delinquent in debts owed the Commission, or is debarred from receiving Federal benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee payments, delinquent debt, and debarment will be examined based on entity's taxpayer identifying number (TIN) supplied when the entity acquired/was assigned an FRN (see 47 CFR 1.8002(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of insufficient payments — handling applications (§1.1910(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications by any entity found not to have paid the proper application or regulatory fee will be handled pursuant to 47 CFR part 1, subpart G. Action will be withheld on applications or requests by any entity found to be delinquent in its debt to the Commission unless otherwise provided in this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entity will be informed that action will be withheld until full payment or arrangement is made and/or the application may be dismissed. Any Commission action taken prior to payment of delinquent non-tax debt is contingent and subject to rescission. Cross-references: §§ 1.1108, 1.1109, 1.1116, and 1.1118.
